Amma says, "The principle of motherhood is as vast and powerful as the universe. With the power of motherhood within her, a woman can influence the entire world". In Gāndhārī's case, we see her failing to influence her children for the better. Her Pratijñā to remain blindfolded arose not from the clarity of thinking but more from an instantaneous emotional response, at an age when she would have had relatively less understanding about the essence, purpose, and comprehensiveness of marriage.
Arjuna's Pratijñā was to kill Jayadratha before sunset. During the Kurukṣetra war, Arjuna's son Abhimanyu was killed on the thirteenth day, which led to this vow.

Droṇācārya constructed a deadly army formation called Cakravyūha. The Pāṇḍavas planned that Abhimanyu would penetrate the army formation, while the other warriors would follow and protect him. But King Jayadratha's unexpected interference prevented the rest of the Pāṇḍava warriors from entering the Cakravyūha. Abhimanyu, however, breached the army formation and killed Duryodhana's son and many other princes. Sadly, breaking all the ethics of Dharmayuddha, Abhimanyu was simultaneously attacked by many powerful warriors of Duryodhana's army. He was killed by a final blow from Duhśāsana son. When Arjuna learned of his son's death, he was filled with anger, and he pledged that he would kill Jayadratha the very next day before sunset.
